final_message:
`wolfi` and `chainguard` no longer crash on ids like `GO-2026-5932`. For those ids, `build_reference_links` now returns only the distro security page link. CVE and GHSA ids keep their current links.

The fix is one line in `src/vunnel/providers/wolfi/parser.py`. The shared helper returns `None` for ids that aren't `CVE-` or `GHSA-` prefixed, so I added `or []` before the `urls.extend(...)` call.

The wolfi and chainguard unit tests pass (16), but only when run with `PYTHONPATH=src`. The plain `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` from CLAUDE.md fails at import with `No module named 'vunnel'`, so I didn't run the full suite. I also didn't add a test for the new case.

I wrote `answer.json` in the repository root with the one-sentence summary.

steps.command: sed -n 55,80p src/vunnel/providers/secureos/parser.py; grep -n "def build_reference_links" -A25 src/vunnel/utils/vulnerability.py; grep -rn "SecDBParser\|def build_reference_links" src | grep -v "^src/vunnel/providers/\(alpine\|secureos\)"

sed -i 's/        urls.extend(vulnerability.build_reference_links(vulnerability_id))/        urls.extend(vulnerability.build_reference_links(vulnerability_id) or [])/' src/vunnel/providers/wolfi/parser.py
echo '{"summary": "Wolfi/chainguard Parser.build_reference_links now tolerates ids without CVE-/GHSA- prefix, returning only the distro security page link."}' > answer.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; ls .venv/bin | head -3; git status --short
